topics.topic: Ownership, consumers, and mapping of active-only uniqueness, history reads, and partial-index enforcement
questions: Which modules own and consume A8's INV-009 after uniqueness means one active ProjectViewerGrant or ProducerProjectGrant per pair? The mapped owner and consumers neither manage those grants nor implement their persistence.

For each of ProjectViewerGrant, StaffProjectAssignment and ProducerProjectGrant, which owner decides the one-active-row invariant, which owner defines active-only pair reads and retained history, and which module implements the partial unique index? State 3 also says application modules own the grants or assignments, repositories hide SQL, and viewer_access_repository owns grant uniqueness.

Which primary owner and consumers own the 2026-11-22 decision that revoked grants and assignments remain as history while a new active record may be created, and where must that decision be added to the ownership mapping?

Which accepted decision and owning module contain the equivalent at-most-one-active rule for `StaffProjectAssignment`, and does A8 still own the viewer and producer uniqueness rules after the Q29 change?
Which modules own and consume A8's INV-009 rule now that viewer and producer grants permit historical revoked rows and require uniqueness only among active rows?
Does `viewer_access_repository` own the rule that only one active grant may exist, or does `viewer_access` own that rule while the repository merely enforces it with a partial unique index?
Which modules own the new partial unique indexes for StaffProjectAssignment and ProducerProjectGrant, and which application modules own the corresponding active-only uniqueness decisions?

quotes: Each accepted decision has one primary owner, the module that holds the decision's central mechanism, and consumers, except the two decisions recorded `cross_cutting` (A22, A26, below).

The SQLite implementation of the `ViewerAccessRepository` port (the port itself is a `models` interface): client viewers, access credentials,
viewer sessions and project grants, with grant uniqueness.
judgement.why: A8 assigns INV-009 to `snapshot_import`, while `viewer_access_repository` independently owns grant uniqueness, so the same decision has two primary owners despite the explicit one-primary-owner rule.

topics.topic: Database migration from pair-wide uniqueness to partial active-row uniqueness for all three record types
questions: How must an existing database remove the old pair-wide UNIQUE constraint, install the partial unique index, preserve revoked rows, and advance its schema revision for all three affected tables?
How is an existing SQLite viewer-grant table with a full UNIQUE `(viewer_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded so that re-granting after revocation actually works?
How is an existing SQLite staff-assignment table with a full UNIQUE `(staff_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded to permit a new assignment after revocation?
How is an existing SQLite producer-grant table with a full UNIQUE `(service_principal_id, project_id)` constraint upgraded to permit a new grant after revocation?

quotes: Owner 2026-11-22 (`open_questions.md` Q29 (a)) reverses the narrowing: a second insert for a pair answered 500 and no administrator could give access again after a revocation. One active grant per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.

Owner 2026-11-22 (`open_questions.md` Q29 (a)) reverses the narrowing: a second insert for a pair answered 500 and no administrator could give access again after a revocation. One active assignment per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.
judgement.why: The transactional upgrade procedure and schema-revision advancement are migration operations and implementation notes, not State 3 module-ownership decisions.

topics.topic: Domain result when concurrent replacement creation loses on the partial unique index
questions: When two administrators concurrently create replacement active records for the same pair, what domain result must the losing operation return when the partial unique index rejects it?

quotes: PortalUnitOfWork.commit: [ORCHESTRATION] Every implementation of PortalUnitOfWork MUST commit the complete write set of the unit of work atomically and exactly once and then close it, so no later call can use it; a failure MUST close it as well and surface as PersistenceError without driver detail.

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero, except in the two reads whose Errors say so:
judgement.why: The later transaction contract requires the losing constraint failure to surface as `PersistenceError`, and the later HTTP policy maps that result to 500.

questions: After a pair has historical revoked records and a new active record, do the viewer, staff-assignment and producer revocation operations identify the active record by pair or identify one exact record by `grant_id` or `assignment_id`, and what must happen to a stale repeated revocation request?

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
